summary: Defines a MIB module, a set of objects for network management with SNMP, for handling circuits that need to appear in a device's interface table. This lets other MIB modules that expect an interface entry work with circuits unchanged. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: A big list of a router's connections only had room for ordinary plugs. This adds a way to put special pretend plugs on the list, so tools that read the list can track them too.

subtitle: A MIB module that lets selected circuits, such as Frame Relay or ATM virtual circuits, get their own row in the interfaces table.

tldr.problem: Many MIB modules, such as routing and RMON, work only on rows of the interfaces table (ifTable), but circuits like Frame Relay and ATM virtual circuits do not get their own row, and the Interfaces Group MIB strongly recommends against adding rows for virtual circuits.
tldr.mechanism: The CIRCUIT-IF-MIB adds a control table (ciCircuitTable) where a manager names a circuit and a flow direction, and the agent then creates a matching ifTable row. A second table (ciIfMapTable) maps the ifIndex back to the circuit.
tldr.outcome: Only the circuits that need an ifIndex are added, so routing and monitoring MIB modules can use them unchanged. The unit metadata says this RFC is updated by RFC 9141.

today: RFC 3201 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists it as updated by RFC 9141. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Problem: Circuits Without an ifIndex
sections.content:
RFC 3201 defines a MIB module (CIRCUIT-IF-MIB) for use with SNMP network management. Its purpose is to manage the insertion of interesting circuit interfaces into the ifTable, the standard table of interfaces on a device.

This matters because other MIB modules need an interface row. The RFC names the routing tables ipCidrRouteTable and ipNetToMediaTable, which act on the ifIndex, and the RMON MIBs, which need an ifIndex as a data source. Circuits such as those in the Frame Relay DTE MIB, the Frame Relay Service MIB and the ATM MIB can be created and deleted there, but none of them creates an ifEntry.

That is deliberate. Not every circuit needs RMON monitoring or routing, and the Interfaces Group MIB (RFC 2863) strongly recommends that rows not be added to the ifTable for virtual circuits. This module resolves the tension by adding rows only for the circuits that need them. It is not limited to ATM and Frame Relay: any circuit defined in a MIB module that lacks its own ifIndex MAY be added.
sections.eli5: A big list of connections had no room for pretend ones, but some tools can only read that list. This adds pretend connections to the list, but only the ones you ask for.

sections.title: Direction-Specific Interfaces
sections.content:
A circuit can carry traffic both ways, and sometimes a manager wants to watch only one way. The RFC notes that monitoring protocols on a circuit with RMON-II (RFC 2021) does not currently capture the direction of the flow. This module lets you define an interface for a specific direction.

The direction is a textual convention called CiFlowDirection with three values: transmit(1) for only transmitted data, receive(2) for only received data, and both(3) for both. Each row in the circuit table is identified by the circuit and the flow, so one circuit can have several interface rows.

If an interface is not both(3), the ifDescr of that interface SHOULD carry text warning operators that it represents only half the traffic on the circuit.
sections.eli5: Think of a two-way street. You can watch only the cars going one way, or both ways. If you only watch one way, the label should say so.

sections.title: Creating, Changing and Destroying Rows
sections.content:
Devices may fill ciCircuitTable automatically as circuits are created or discovered. Otherwise a manager creates rows by hand: first locate or create the circuit on the device, then create a row in ciCircuitTable for each flow type needed. An entry describing the circuit MUST already exist in some table before a row is created. The object identifier used MUST be the lexicographically smallest accessible one that fully describes the circuit.

The RFC gives examples of where to look. For a logical port of ifType frameRelay(32), circuits are in frCircuitTable of the Frame Relay DTE MIB. For frameRelayService(44), they are in frPVCEndptTable of the Frame Relay Service MIB. For aal5(49), they are in aal5VccTable of the ATM MIB.

When a row becomes active(1), the agent adds a row to the ifTable and to the map table, and chooses the ifIndex itself according to the rules of the ifTable. Setting ciCircuitStatus to destroy(6) removes the associated rows, which MAY trigger further deletions in other tables. Rows MUST also be removed as soon as the underlying circuit is found to no longer exist. Nothing can be changed once a row is active, so there is no modification procedure. Persistence SHOULD follow the rules of the underlying MIB module.
sections.eli5: You first make sure the real connection exists, then ask for a list entry for it. When the connection goes away, its entry is removed too.

sections.title: The Two Tables and the Interface Row
sections.content:
The module has two main tables. ciCircuitTable is the central control table. It maps a circuit to its ifIndex and forces an ifTable row into existence. It is indexed by ciCircuitObject (a RowPointer to the circuit) and ciCircuitFlow, and holds the status, the assigned ciCircuitIfIndex, the creation time and the storage type. A row here MUST exist before a row can exist in any other table of the module. ciIfMapTable, indexed by ifIndex, maps back to the circuit and flow. Two scalar objects track changes: ciIfLastChange and ciIfNumActive.

The RFC also says what the interface row looks like. The agent defines ifIndex. The ifType depends on the circuit: frDlciEndPt(193) for Frame Relay virtual circuits and atmVciEndPt(194) for ATM virtual circuits. If the circuit is to be used in RMON, propVirtual(53) SHOULD NOT be used. ifPhysAddress is always a zero-length octet string, and ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable, ifPromiscuousMode and ifConnectorPresent are set to false(2). The link up/down trap is off because circuits often have their own notification mechanism, and enabling it would double the notifications.

Counters such as ifInOctets and ifOutErrors MUST NOT be supported, and return noSuchInstance, if the device keeps no statistics on the circuit.
sections.eli5: One table says which pretend plug belongs to which real connection. The other works backwards. The new list entry gets simple, fixed answers for things that make no sense for a pretend plug.

sections.title: Stacking Circuits with ifStackTable
sections.content:
The RFC shows by example how the ifStackTable records which interface sits on which. In the Frame Relay example, three circuit interfaces (type 193) sit on a frameRelayService interface (type 44), which sits on a V.35 physical interface (type 33). The index values are 1, 2 and 3 for the circuits, 4 for the service and 5 for the physical layer.

The stack table then pairs higher and lower layers: 0 over 1, 2 and 3 at the top, each of 1, 2 and 3 over 4, then 4 over 5, and 5 over 0. The ATM example works the same way with three atmVciEndPt interfaces (type 194) on aal5 (type 49), on atm (type 37), on a DS3 interface (type 30).
sections.eli5: It is like a stack of boxes. Each pretend plug sits on a bigger box, which sits on the real wire, and the table writes down who sits on whom.

sections.title: Security and IANA Notes
sections.content:
Objects with read-write or read-create access may be sensitive. Allowing SET operations without protection can hurt network operations. SNMPv1 by itself is not secure, and even on a secure network (for example one using IPSec) nothing controls who may GET or SET the objects. The RFC recommends that implementers consider the SNMPv3 framework, specifically the User-based Security Model and the View-based Access Control Model. It is then the user's responsibility to configure the SNMP entity so only legitimate principals can read or change these objects.

For IANA, new ifType values defined for this module SHOULD take the form ***EndPt, like frDlciEndPt(193) and atmVciEndPt(194).
sections.eli5: If anyone can change the list, they can break things. So lock it so only the right people can touch it.
